module purpose: neorv32_fifo buffers input words in a parameterized FIFO, updates internal read and write positions on accepted read and write requests, and returns the selected stored word on rdata_o. It also reports fill level and free/available/half-full status, with clear_i and rstn_i reinitializing queue state and optional synchronous read/status timing.

use-case flows.value: accepted write request qualified by FIFO_SAFE and current free status
enqueue the input word into FIFO storage and advance the write pointer
accepted read request qualified by FIFO_SAFE and current available status
advance the read pointer and present the selected stored FIFO word on rdata_o
FIFO fill level and free/available/half-full status
pointer state cleared by rstn_i or clear_i, and storage/status forced to zero in the configured reset branches

conceptual assets.concept: Write-admission decision -- whether an asserted write request is allowed to update FIFO storage
conceptual assets.reasoning: Line 65 computes we from we_i and, when FIFO_SAFE is true, free. That decision gates the write-pointer next state at line 82 and the storage updates at lines 134-135, 149-150, 170-171 and 183-184. Integrity is established because enqueueing data and advancing the FIFO must occur exactly when this implemented predicate is true. Availability is also established conditionally: when we_i is asserted and the implemented free-space condition permits it, the decision is produced and used by the next clocked updates.

conceptual assets.concept: Read-admission decision -- whether an asserted read request is allowed to advance the dequeue position
conceptual assets.reasoning: Line 64 computes re from re_i and, when FIFO_SAFE is true, avail. That decision gates the read-pointer next state at line 83, is copied into r_pnt at line 77 through r_nxt, and in the asynchronous large-depth branch also drives the delayed read pointer captured at line 210 and used to select rdata_o at line 213. Integrity is established because dequeue progression must follow this implemented request/availability predicate; otherwise the module skips, repeats, or exposes the wrong entries. Availability is also established conditionally when re_i is asserted and the implemented data-available condition permits it.

conceptual assets.concept: Buffered FIFO payload data -- the word written into the queue and later returned on the read data port
conceptual assets.reasoning: Accepted writes store wdata_i into fifo_reg in the single-entry configuration (lines 135, 171) or into fifo_mem in the multi-entry configuration (lines 150, 184). The read path returns that stored value on rdata_o by copying fifo_reg (lines 201, 232) or by deriving from fifo_mem at the addressed entry (lines 213, 241). Integrity is established because the enqueue and read-out flows depend on rdata_o reflecting the value the FIFO stored. Availability is also established conditionally: once a word is stored, the configured read path presents the selected stored entry until that location is overwritten or the addressing state changes.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO position state -- the stored read and write positions that preserve entry order
conceptual assets.reasoning: The queue position is held in w_pnt and r_pnt, reset at lines 73-74 and updated from w_nxt and r_nxt at lines 76-77. clear_i forces both next values to zero at lines 82-83; otherwise w_nxt and r_nxt increment or retain the current pointers. This state selects where multi-entry writes land (lines 150, 184) and which multi-entry word is read (line 241); in the asynchronous large-depth branch r_pnt_ff captures r_nxt at line 210 and supplies the read index at line 213. Integrity is established because corrupt position state changes FIFO ordering, occupancy, and addressed storage locations. Availability is also established conditionally by the implemented clear/update rules on each rising clock edge with reset inactive.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO occupancy status -- the reported level and the free, available, and half-full indications
conceptual assets.reasoning: For multi-entry FIFOs, the module computes level from w_pnt minus r_pnt and derives half from level or full at lines 95-96, with full and empty decided from pointer comparisons at lines 92-94. For single-entry FIFOs, the alternative equations are at lines 102-106. free and avail are then derived at lines 110-111. These values leave the entity through level_o (lines 116-117) and through free_o, avail_o, and half_o either combinationally (lines 217-219) or registered in FIFO_RSYNC mode (lines 249-256). When FIFO_SAFE is true, free and avail also qualify writes and reads at lines 65 and 64. Integrity is established because correct flow-control reporting and safe-mode admission checks depend on these computed status values. Availability is also established for the configured output mode because each status output is continuously driven or updated on the clock.
